TODAY — BOLDER

Same content, a point of view. Four changes, all borrowed as principles rather than pixels:

1. The sidebar is gone. It made a reading app look like a dashboard and took a fifth of the screen away from the writing.

2. Headlines go 16px → 30px and the date goes to 68px. A digest of five things can afford to be set like a publication instead of a table.

3. One rule generates the type: big is Geist, small is Geist Mono, nothing in between. Every piece of metadata is mono; every piece of content is sans.

4. Utilities become underlined text in the corners, and the only component on screen is the floating pill. One saturated colour (#ff4d1c) appears in exactly two places — the live status dot and the rank of item 01.

STILL OPEN

· The accent is a placeholder — it should probably be yours, not a colour I picked.
· "Switch to compact?" implies a second density mode. Worth building, or cut it?
· This costs vertical space: five stories no longer fit above the fold. For a once-a-day read I think that is the right trade, but it is a trade.

DevNews — five screens, direction C refined.

Hierarchy comes from type scale, weight and one hairline — not from boxes. Palette is strictly your existing zero-chroma tokens; the only saturated colour is the three OAuth brand marks.

Geometry is lifted from the shadcn primitives already installed: badge h-20px / rounded-4xl / 12px, button h-32px / rounded-10px, card ring-1 at foreground/10. Sample headlines and scores are invented.

TODAY
Rank, title and score share one baseline; source metadata drops below the summary so the writing leads. Rows are hairline-divided rather than carded.

PREFERENCES
Selected topics invert to solid white rather than tinting. Sliders are 3px rails — the same treatment as the source-mix bars, so one idea is reused instead of two being invented.

SIGN IN
Split layout: form left, the three-step explanation right on a slightly lifted ground (#0d0d0d). This is where the old Hero copy went now that / is gated.

QUIET DAY
A real answer, not a broken page. The date header stays so the day is still legible as a day; the escape hatch to the rejects sits under it.
